Unreal Engine Networking × sa_std Network Surface Census and Gap Table

This page is a two-side census done on 2026-10-27 (the Unreal line of the cross-language std census batch): it extracts the surface of Unreal Engine 5.8's networking system into an inventory, then compares and classifies it item by item against sa_std's network surface. First, the characterization: UE's networking system is not a general net std, but a game replication (Replication) system — its center of gravity is synchronizing the state deltas of game objects to multiple clients; only the bottom-most Sockets transport layer is truly isomorphic to a general std. The comparison methodology of this page is therefore layered: the transport layer is compared capability by capability, the replication layer only registers its model and prerequisites, and finally it draws the line between what sa_std should fill in and what engine-specific surfaces a general std should not absorb. All entries come from the scripts and inventories checked in with the page (tools/unreal_net_census/), are re-runnable, and no conclusions are drawn from impressions. Pages in the same batch: Android net × sa_std Census, Rust std × sa_std Census.

Source Grades and Coverage Boundaries

  • Grade 1 (signature level): official API reference class pages — class names, header files, and signature candidates are all extracted by script from the page tables. This line deeply extracted 21 flagship classes, and used 5 module index pages (Sockets / PacketHandler / IrisCore / ReplicationGraph / OnlineSubsystem) for class-level inventory.
  • Grade 2 (documentation level): official concept documentation (networking overview, RPC, property replication, dormancy, four Iris articles, Replication Graph, Oodle Network, 14 pages in total) — can prove that concepts/models/terms exist, but is not signature evidence.
  • Unverifiable: UIpNetDriver / UIpConnection soft-404 at all three candidate paths in the API reference; FFastArraySerializer is likewise not in the API reference index (documentation-level evidence only); FNetSerializer's class page exists and its header file is verifiable, but its in-page signature table extraction is 0, so it is unverifiable at method level. All three are registered honestly in the classification table, with no signatures filled in.
  • Iris maturity: the official Iris component documentation describes itself as an Experimental feature and advises shipping caution; this page's Iris conclusions are understood as “UE5's new architecture, still evolving”.
  • SA-side counting methodology: .sai takes @extern declarations, .sa/.sal/.sla take sa_* symbol tokens, deduplicated by file group; this is a symbol-surface methodology and does not claim item-by-item semantic matching.

Classification Summary Table

The four classification grades use the batch's unified methodology: existing equivalent (sa_std already covers it, including correspondences of different shapes), directly mappable (the semantics can land directly in sa_std, just not done yet), needs modeling (requires modeling prerequisites such as handles/state machines/ host object models), model mismatch (engine-specific or platform service surfaces that a general std should not absorb, with a reason given for each). There is also 1 unverifiable entry listed separately, not entering the four grades' denominator. 36 entries in total, of which 35 are archived classifications: existing equivalent 5 (14%), directly mappable 8 (23%), needs modeling 18 (51%), model mismatch 4 (11%). The structure is clear at a glance: the transport layer is basically aligned, with gaps concentrated and small; almost everything above NetDriver is “needs modeling” — what they lack is not functions, but a whole host object model.

Replication Model Dedicated Section (Registration Only, Not Entering the Closing Shortlist)

UE classic replication's work unit is “object + reflected property table”. The server maintains, for each replicated object, a shadow state (shadow buffer); each frame FRepLayout does an incremental diff of the current values against the shadow values (its measured signatures include DiffProperties, CreateShadowBuffer, GenerateChecksum), and sends only the changed properties, filtered by replication conditions (the COND_* condition family: owner-only, initial-only, simulated-side-only, etc.) and relevance (observer distance culling, priority, update frequency, the dormancy state machine), through UNetConnection's bunch queues (fragmentation, ack, reordering; measured signatures include WriteBitsToSendBuffer, GetMaxSingleBunchSizeBits, IsInternalAck) to each client; after the client applies the values, OnRep_ callbacks are triggered (RepNotify, mentioned 45 times on the documentation page). Function calls go through the three RPC kinds (Server / Client / NetMulticast, with reliability flags and validation functions), object identity is anchored by the NetGUID mapping maintained by FNetGUIDCache (PackageMap), arrays have a dedicated Fast Array delta protocol, and spatial relevance can be precomputed by the Replication Graph.

This model's prerequisites are: reflected property metadata, UObject lifecycles and ownership trees, and level/world spatial models. sa_std is a general standard library with no host objects, and has none of the three. The replication framework as a whole is therefore classified as “needs modeling” and registered only: if a replication framework is done in the SA ecosystem in the future, it should be a framework layer built on top of std (by analogy with the plug-in layering), and its design inputs are exactly the model pieces registered in this section — RepLayout-style diff+shadow state, the condition family, dormancy, relevance grading, GUID mapping, Fast Array deltas. The only foundation piece that sinks to the std layer is bit-level packing, already on the shortlist.

Iris Dedicated Section

Iris is UE5's new replication system (officially self-described as Experimental). Its biggest difference from classic replication is state ownership: Iris keeps, inside the replication system, quantized copies of all replicated state (the component documentation describes it as “a full copy of all replicated state data in a quantized form”); game-layer objects are mapped through UReplicationBridge to internal Net Objects, identified by Net Ref Handles (handles of the same concept as NetGUID); state is organized by Replication Fragments and serialized and sent down through Data Streams (corresponding to classic replication's channels); serialization goes through the type-registered FNetSerializer system (the header file Net/Iris/Public/Iris/Serialization/NetSerializer.h is verified), and the glossary also has entries such as Net Bit Stream Reader, Net Blob, and Fast Array Replication Fragment. The IrisCore module index reaches 402 classes, the fastest-expanding part of UE's network surface.

The implication for sa_std is the same as classic replication: the model is registered and does not enter the closing shortlist. But two of Iris's design orientations are worth referencing when designing the upper-layer framework — decoupling state copies from game objects (the replication system does not look back into game object memory) and serializers registered per type and carrying their own quantized variants. The former is naturally compatible with SA's handle/ ownership model, and the latter connects directly with this page's shortlist items of bit-level packing + quantization codecs.

Reverse Note: What SA Already Has and UE's Core Network Surface Does Not

The comparison is one-directional (using UE as the reference to find SA gaps), but the reverse facts must be recorded honestly: the application-layer protocol surfaces built into sa_std — HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 clients and servers, WebSocket, TLS clients and servers, the QUIC capability surface, the SSH declaration surface, and netx's io_uring reactor and broadcasting — have no counterparts in UE's core networking system; UE's corresponding capabilities live in the plug-in layer (the HTTP module, OnlineSubsystem and its backend services). That is, under the “usable without any plug-in” methodology, sa_std's built-in network surface is more complete than UE's core network stack; UE's lead is only in the replication system, and that is a framework layer, not an std layer.

Priority Shortlist for Closing Gaps

  1. Bit-level packing reads/writes (bit writer/reader): compact encoding primitives that are not byte-aligned. On the UE side, everything from bunch send buffers to Iris's Net Bit Stream takes it as the foundation; sa_std's network/encoding surface has zero bit-level symbol hits in a full-surface search. A small surface with clear semantics, reusable by general protocol codecs as well — the top priority of this batch.
  2. A standalone DNS resolution surface: synchronous/asynchronous resolution + result objects + a host name cache, decoupled from transport. On the UE side, ISocketSubsystem has the GetAddressInfo/GetAddressInfoAsync/FResolveInfo family; SA currently has only resolution embedded in connect and one reverse query. This corroborates the Android line census's “0 dns hits” conclusion; it is a surface commonly missing across many std comparisons.
  3. A NetQuantize-style quantization codec family: vectors/rotations/scalars quantized and packed at configurable precision (bit width), corresponding to the grading idea of FVector_NetQuantize/10/100. Pure encoding pieces, depending on no game object model.
  4. Three datagram enhancements: RecvMulti-style bulk packet reception, pktinfo carried with packets (destination address/interface), and packet timestamps. SA's UDP surface is already very complete (multicast/vectored are all there); these three are the only fine-grained gaps left for high-throughput and multi-homed datagram services.
  5. The local network information surface: local adapter enumeration, multihome addresses, and (merged with the AT line's recommendation) routing information. On the UE side, GetLocalAdapterAddresses/GetMultihomeAddress are verifiable; SA has only two points: hostname and the listener's local address.
  6. A network fault injection shim: programmable injection of packet loss/latency/jitter/reordering, for protocol and reliability layer testing. UE has a full set of emulation settings at the NetDriver layer (partly unverifiable at signature level, registered on mixed-grade evidence). Small to implement, high testing value.

Everything on the UE surface beyond the shortlist — the replication framework, Iris, the Replication Graph, the PacketHandler component chain, NetGUID mapping, OnlineSubsystem — registers only the model and does not enter sa_std's gap-closing plan.

Re-running

Scripts and inventories are in tools/unreal_net_census/: fetch_ue_pages.py (source notes and the fetch inventory, including the gated repository measurement record), extract_ue_api.py (API reference page and module index extraction, producing ue_api_surface.tsv / ue_module_index.tsv / ue_doc_keywords.tsv), extract_sa_net.py (SA-side extraction, producing sa_net_surface.tsv), ue_gap_items.tsv (36 classification entries, each with evidence and notes), gen_gap_table.py (generates summary.json and this page's tables from the entry table). The fetched raw HTML is not checked in (size and redistribution considerations) and can be re-fetched with the fetch script; dev.epicgames.com's page content evolves with versions, so re-run numbers may drift slightly.
